title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time Remake Cancelled Six Years After Debut - NewsBreak
text:
By Zak Wojnar ,
6 hours ago
One of the oldest and most respected franchises in gaming history, Prince of Persia has seen its ups and downs since the original game made its grand debut way back in 1989. After fizzling out following the disappointment of 1999's Prince of Persia 3D (one of many game series that struggled to transition from 2D to 3D in the 1990s), the series was rebooted with 2003's Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time, which spawned multiple sequels and even a feature film adaptation starring Jake Gyllenhaal as a decidedly whitewashed version of the title character.
In any event, the series ultimately fell out of favor, with Ubisoft instead championing its spiritual successor, the Assassin's Creed series. In fact, the legend goes that the original Assassin's Creed started out as a Prince of Persia spin-off before evolving into its own thing. Despite the ongoing success of Assassin's Creed, fans still clamored for the return of Prince of Persia, and their wishes came true in 2020, with the announcement of a full remake of The Sands of Time.
Six years later, the saga of the Prince of Persia remake is over. The game has been cancelled by Ubisoft as part of a restructuring that cancelled several unannounced games and delays to multiple in-development titles.
While this is a sad end for Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake, the writing has been on the wall for years. When the game was announced back in 2020, it was expected to release sometime in 2021. However, following the lackluster initial announcement, the game went into development hell, suffering numerous delays to the point where Ubisoft Montreal, the team behind the original 2003 game, was brought in to take over development duties for the project. In 2024, the remake was re-unveiled, this time to a more positive reception and an expected release date in 2026. Alas, that release would never come to pass.
I wonder how close Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time was to the finish line. Would it have been ready to come out before the end of 2026? After funding no fewer than six years of development for the game, would it have killed Ubisoft to bring the game over the finish line? I'm sure it's just a matter of time before we hear some behind-the-scenes stories of Prince of Persia's troubled development cycle.
Through it all, Prince of Persia will go on, one way or another. In the statement announcing the cancellation, "The Prince of Persia Team" at Ubisoft Montreal said that the game's cancellation does not mean they're stepping away from the franchise. Maybe they'll be able to take the work they've done thus far and apply it to a brand new game. After all, brand new games are usually more exciting than remakes, right?
